Usually the difference is theft vs robbery. Theft has a very low minimum sentence. Robbery is 7 years where I live. The only difference is if someone is present to feel threatened.

Robbery/larceny typically is when there is use of force is involved. Burglary is when no force is used, usually better used when someone is not around or not forcing them, i.e. breaking into a house and stealing when nobody is home or sleeping.

Since an employee is present, he will be charged with robbery. In most places burglary is considered a rather minor crime, whereas robbery generally carries a 7 year minimum sentence (at least in my state). If there are any people present at all, the prosecutors generally have a very easy time going for a robbery conviction.

I know of a recent case where a man stole a cash register and ran away. Literally grabbed it off the counter, cut the electric cord, and ran away. Got 7 years for robbery because the attendant was present. Didn't threaten them, didn't demand money from them, just grabbed something and ran. Theft over $1000 would have got him a few years probation probably. Robbery is hard time.

In a lot of places, it is only burglary when there are no people in the place being targeted. Even if it can be proven that the assailants believed they'd find resistance (i.e. they arm themselves with weapons because they expect to run into people) they can be charged with robbery. The second that employee walked into frame the charges got upgraded from burglary to robbery. If he threatens the employee with his screwdriver then he could be charged with armed or aggravated robbery depending on the severity of his actions.

You'd need to check the revised codes for your state and possibly local municipality to know for sure what constitutes a robbery or burglary in your area.
